title: Teleportation through time-varying channels: threshold geometry and a complete-positivity bound on non-Markovian backflow
abstract: A Bell pair distributed through a link that combines amplitude damping with dephasing at time-dependent rates has dynamics that separate into a fixed part and a moving one. The negativity, fully entangled fraction, discord, and average teleportation fidelity depend on time only through the accumulated damping parameters $p(t)$ and $q(t)$. Every threshold is therefore a curve fixed in the unit square, and the rates select nothing but a trajectory across it. The Horodecki fidelity formula $\bar{F} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{6}\mathrm{Tr}|T|$ covers one- and two-sided exposure alike: the condition $\det T \leq 0$ under which it takes this form holds throughout the unit square for both. Under symmetric two-sided noise the entanglement vanishes when $p+q\geq1$, where the exact relation $\bar{F}^{2s}=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3}\mathcal{N}_{2s}$ ties disentanglement and the loss of quantum advantage to the same instant. One-sided exposure admits no finite-time sudden death for any rate profile, and the discord stays strictly positive throughout the open square, so the distributed state can be separable, useless for teleportation, and still nonclassical. For harmonically modulated rates, complete positivity caps the backflow at one modulation period of static decay, $ΔΓ_{k}\leq2πγ_{k,0}/Ω$, equivalently at a modulation depth $ξ_{k}\leq4.6033$ independent of $Ω$. Inside that window the trajectory reverses, producing finite intervals of restored quantum advantage and entanglement sudden birth.
summary: This paper analyzes the degradation of quantum entanglement and teleportation fidelity when qubits pass through time-varying decoherence channels. By mapping resource thresholds onto a fixed parameter space, the authors derive bounds on how much coherence can 'backflow' due to modulation. The results show that while resources decay overall, controlled modulation can lead to temporary revivals of quantum advantage.
main_problem: The study investigates quantum teleportation fidelity through time-varying, non-Markovian decoherence channels.
main_result: The analysis establishes a complete positivity bound on the backflow of coherence ($\Delta\Gamma_k \le 2\pi\gamma_{k,0}/\Omega$) and shows that modulation can induce transient revival of quantum advantage.
method: The authors model decoherence using time-local master equations, analyzing resource degradation by mapping thresholds onto a fixed $(p, q)$ plane.
model_or_system: The system involves teleporting an unknown qubit state via a shared entangled pair passing through a link combining amplitude damping and dephasing at time-dependent rates. The dynamics are parameterized by two accumulated damping factors, $p(t)$ and $q(t)$.
key_observables: Negativity ($N$), Fully Entangled Fraction ($f$), Quantum Discord ($D$), and Average Teleportation Fidelity ($ ar{F}$).
important_parameters: Accumulated damping parameters $p(t)$ and $q(t)$; modulation depth $\xi_k$; the critical threshold condition $p+q \ge 1$ for entanglement vanishing.
main_assumptions: The time evolution separates into a fixed part and a moving one, depending only on accumulated damping parameters $p(t)$ and $q(t)$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the rate profiles ($\gamma_1(t), \Gamma_1(t)$) across static, fast, and modulated regimes. Figure 2 plots resource measures like negativity and fidelity over time for one-sided exposure.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the dynamics using accumulated parameters $p(t)$ and $q(t)$, then analyzes different noise geometries (one-sided vs. two-sided), deriving key bounds from complete positivity, and finally discussing resource revival phenomena under harmonic modulation.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical bounds on how quantum resources can be temporarily restored or enhanced by time-varying environments, which is crucial for designing robust quantum communication protocols.
